docs.title: IoTwin
docs.text: IoTwin is a modular open-source platform for digital twin simulation, visualization, and IoT system integration. Its goal is to bridge physical embedded systems and virtual simulations within a unified environment suitable for research, testing, and real-world development.

docs.title: 💡 Overview
docs.text:
IoTwin consists of two main components:

  1. IoTwin Core (Backend + Simulators)
  2. Written in C++ with a modular architecture
  3. Provides simulation logic for electrical systems, sensors, and communication modules

  4. Built using CMake for cross-platform compatibility

  5. IoTwin Visualizer (Unreal Engine Project)

  6. Provides real-time visualization of simulated devices and environments
  7. Supports interactive scenarios and rule-based simulations
  8. Useful for training, validation, and system analysis

docs.title: 🧭 Goals
docs.text:
• Provide a flexible development and testing environment for embedded and IoT systems
  • Enable digital twin modeling for realistic device behavior
  • Ensure extensibility, allowing new modules, devices, and visualizations to be added easily

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Follow the Build Instructions to set up your system.
  2. Build and run the IoTwin Core simulator.
  3. Open the IoTwin Visualizer in Unreal Engine to view and interact with simulations.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Choice of Documentation System
docs.text:
Date: 2025-10-07 Context: The project requires long-term maintainable documentation combining developer guides, architecture decisions, and auto-generated API references.

Decision: Use MkDocs + Material for the general documentation and Doxygen for API docs. ADRs will be written in Markdown under docs/adr/.

Consequences: - Single source of truth (Markdown in Git) - Fully static deployable site - Version-controlled documentation with minimal tooling overhead

docs.title: Build Instructions
docs.text: This document describes how to set up, build, and run the IoTwin project on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

docs.title: General Requirements
docs.text: Tool / Library Minimum Version Notes CMake 3.20+ Required for building the C++ components Git — To clone the repository C++ Compiler C++20-compatible GCC ≥ 11, Clang ≥ 13, or MSVC 2022 Python 3 3.8+ Used for helper scripts

docs.title: 5. Run
docs.text:
The built binaries will be located in: 

build/bin/

docs.title: 🎮 Setting up the IoTwin Visualizer (Unreal Engine)
1. Install Unreal Engine
docs.text:
IoTwin requires Unreal Engine 5.3 or later.

Linux/macOS: Install via Epic Games Launcher Windows: Install via Epic Games Launcher.

If building from source, follow the Unreal Engine GitHub setup guide

docs.title: 2. Open the Unreal Project
docs.text:
In the repository: 

src/ue/IoTwin/IoTwin.uproject
Open this file in Unreal Engine. On first open, Unreal will prompt to rebuild missing modules — confirm with Yes.

docs.title: 3. Configure the Visualizer
docs.text: The Unreal project communicates with the IoTwin Core via local networking interfaces (default: TCP localhost). Ensure the backend is running before starting the simulation in the editor.
